title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

reading.body:
This is an impersonation carried out with synthetic video. A person in the Ards and north Down area saw what appeared to be a well known financial figure promoting an investment with large returns, and the video supplied the credibility that the investment itself did not have. The fraud then moved off the public video and into a private WhatsApp conversation, which is where the money was actually taken.

The failure sits at the point where a viewer decides whether the person on screen is real. Nothing in the reporting shows that the video was checked against the actual figure, and the PSNI did not name the celebrity, so the impersonation was not caught at the moment it mattered. Catching it would have required verifying who was behind the endorsement rather than trusting the footage, and checking Financial Conduct Authority authorisation before any money moved. The later steps, opening several online accounts, granting remote access to a computer and borrowing money, were all presented as help, and each one depended on the victim believing the first video was genuine.

What is not established is who the celebrity was, who made the video, or whether anyone has been arrested or charged. The PSNI described the fraud as sophisticated, and that is a police characterisation of the case, not a finding against any named person. The similar scams involving Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett were seen by BBC News NI and are not evidence that those individuals were involved in this incident.

reports.title: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity

summary:
A person in the Ards and north Down area lost £250,000 after an AI generated video scam. The Police Service of Northern Ireland said the victim saw what looked like a video of a well known financial figure promoting an investment with large returns. The PSNI did not name the celebrity. BBC News NI has seen similar scams using financial experts such as Martin Lewis, Peter Jones and Steven Bartlett.

After a small initial investment, the victim was contacted on WhatsApp and urged to pay more. The fraudsters persuaded them to open several online accounts and gave remote access to their computer, saying they were helping. Police called it sophisticated and said the victim was encouraged to borrow money, with funds sent to criminal controlled accounts. Police advised people to verify who they deal with and check Financial Conduct Authority authorisation, and a Scamwise official urged people to stop and check and families to discuss fraud.
title_en: Victim loses £250k after scammers use AI video of 'well-known' celebrity
